messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• Rural roads: 55 mph unless posted otherwise. | Speed limits can be lower in construction zones or school zones. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑seat or booster.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑seat child‑seat. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations can lead to a $50 fine and points on the license. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• For commercial drivers, the limit is 0.04 %.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” policy for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %). | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks.
• Stop signs require a full stop before proceeding. | Failure to yield can result in a $50 fine and points. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Drivers must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Must remain stopped until the bus’s stop sign is lowered. | Violations can lead to a $200 fine and points. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle is turning left. | Unsafe lane changes can result in a $50 fine and points. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | Violations can also lead to towing. | | **Traffic Signal Violations** | • Running a red light or stop sign is a $50 fine.
• Failing to obey a flashing yellow light can result in a $50 fine. | Points are added to the driver’s record. | | **Points System** | • Accumulating 4 points in 12 months can lead to a license suspension.
• 6 points in 24 months can result in a 30‑day suspension. | Points are tracked by the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS). | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Vehicles must be registered annually.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Failure to register or inspect can result in a $50 fine. | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | Driving without insurance can lead to license suspension and a $200 fine. | | **Special Situations** | • **Construction Zones**: Speed limits may be reduced to 20–30 mph.
• **Towing**: Must use a tow truck or a vehicle with a tow hitch.
• **Commercial Vehicles**: Additional regulations for size, weight, and driver hours. | Violations can lead to higher fines and points. | ### How to Stay Updated - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** website: [https://www.dps.texas.gov](https://www.dps.texas.gov) - **Texas Transportation Code**: Available online for detailed statutes. - **Local County Ordinances**: Some counties have additional traffic rules (e.g., speed limits in specific zones). ### Quick Tips 1. **Always obey posted signs and signals.** 2. **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. 3. **Check your vehicle’s registration and insurance status** before driving. 4. **Keep an eye on speed limits**—they can change in construction or school zones. If you need more specific information (e.g., penalties for a particular violation or how to appeal a ticket), let me know!
